credits-pipeline.alt: Diagram showing that finding an email costs one Snov.io credit and verifying it costs another, so one usable verified contact costs about two credits.
credits-pipeline.caption: How credits turn into usable contacts. One credit finds an address, a second verifies it — so a finished contact costs about two credits.

cost-per-lead.alt: Bar chart of approximate cost per verified lead by Snov.io plan: about 8 cents on Starter falling to about 1.5 cents on the largest tier.
cost-per-lead.caption: Approximate cost per verified contact, calculated as plan price ÷ half the credit allowance. Higher tiers are roughly five times cheaper per contact.

verification-results.alt: Flow diagram of email verification outcomes: valid addresses are safe to send, invalid should be deleted, catch-all should be limited, and unknown should be retried rather than treated as valid.
verification-results.caption: What verification actually returns. Only "valid" is safe to send freely; catch-all and unknown are the two results that quietly damage deliverability.

deliverability-stack.alt: Stack diagram showing four layers that decide inbox placement — SPF DKIM and DMARC authentication, domain warm-up, list quality, and engagement — with verification covering only the list quality layer.
deliverability-stack.caption: Verification only fixes one layer. Inbox placement depends on authentication, warm-up, list quality and engagement together.

email-patterns.alt: Table of common business email address patterns such as first.last and first initial plus last name, with an example address for each.
email-patterns.caption: Reading a domain’s address pattern from one confirmed address is faster than guessing. Verify per address — patterns can differ by office.
